findings.message: Public check failed: input '# ##' yields title '##' where expected empty title ''. The candidate's new pattern keeps a leading-only hash run in the text group, so a heading whose entire title is a separated closing hash run is no longer stripped.

The fix only handles the terminal-separated hash run via (?:(?<=[ \t])...), leaving a hash-only title unstripped because the regex has no way to strip a leading hash run. The baseline's '[ \t]*#*' stripped it. This is the root cause of the observed '# ##' failure and may affect other edge inputs (e.g., '# ####', '# ### ##') that the fixed public set does not cover.

Three of four public cases passed ('# C#', '# C# #', '# Title #'), confirming the attached-hash literal behavior and the separated-closer removal for non-empty titles work. Only the empty-title edge case fails. This is a partial, not total, failure of the contract.

outstanding: Behavior for hash-only title with trailing whitespace (e.g., '# ## ') and multiple hash runs (e.g., '# ## ###') is not covered by the fixed public inputs; not verified.
No independent verification that fence exclusion, section boundaries, and find_heading/find_section semantics remain unchanged, though the diff shows those paths are untouched.

requests: Add a regression test for a hash-only title (e.g., '# ##' expected title ''), and verify the empty-title and trailing-whitespace edge cases.
Re-run the public check on a corrected candidate before re-review.
conclusion.summary: The candidate changes only _ATX_HEADING_PATTERN in MarkdownFile (src/devtools/resources/filesystem/models/markdown/file.py), which satisfies the 'only the existing authorized model file may change' requirement. The new pattern correctly preserves attached literal hashes ('# C#' -> 'C#') and strips separated terminal closing hashes for non-empty titles ('# C# #' -> 'C#'), fixing the primary corruption reported in the task. However, the public check fails on the '# ##' case: expected empty title, actual '##'. The candidate's pattern does not strip a hash-only title, regressing the baseline behavior (baseline '[ \t]*#*' stripped it). Since the task explicitly requires preserving empty titles and the current owner's title contract, this is a blocking defect. Disposition: reject. Note: this is a factual code recommendation against the public contract only; formal acceptance/custody records are unavailable in this calibration and are not being asserted here.
